subject: math
cluster: Work with radicals and integer exponents
intro: These problems take two steps: operate on the leading digits and operate on the exponents. Divide leading digits and subtract exponents to find 'how many times as much', convert small numbers to negative powers of 10, and estimate products by multiplying digits and adding exponents. Renormalize your answer so the leading factor is a single digit when needed.

items.prompt: A blue whale has a mass of about $2 \times 10^{5}$ kg. A house cat has a mass of about $4 \times 10^{0}$ kg. About how many times as massive as the cat is the whale?

steps: Write the comparison as a quotient: $\dfrac{2 \times 10^{5}}{4 \times 10^{0}}$.
Renormalize so the leading factor is a single digit: $0.5 \times 10^{5} = 5 \times 10^{4}$.
The whale is $5 \times 10^{4} = 50{,}000$ times as massive as the cat.

items.prompt: The width of a human hair is about $0.00009$ m. Write this measurement as a single digit times an integer power of 10.

steps: The number is less than 1, so the power of 10 will be negative.
Move the decimal point to the right until it sits just after the first nonzero digit: $0.00009 \to 9$.
Count the places moved: $5$ places to the right, so the exponent is $-5$.
Write it in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form: $9 \times 10^{-5}$ m.

items.prompt: A school district has about $3 \times 10^{4}$ students, and each student uses about $5 \times 10^{2}$ sheets of paper per year. Estimate the total number of sheets the district uses per year. Write your answer as a single digit times a power of 10.

steps: Renormalize so the leading factor is a single digit: $15 \times 10^{6} = 1.5 \times 10^{7}$.
The district uses about $1.5 \times 10^{7}$ sheets per year.

items.prompt: The Earth is about $1 \times 10^{8}$ km from the Sun, and Mercury is about $5 \times 10^{7}$ km from the Sun. About how many times as far from the Sun as Mercury is the Earth?

steps: Write the comparison as a quotient: $\dfrac{1 \times 10^{8}}{5 \times 10^{7}}$.
The Earth is about $2$ times as far from the Sun as Mercury.

items.prompt: The mass of a grain of sand is about $7 \times 10^{-6}$ kg. The mass of a single bacterium is about $1 \times 10^{-12}$ kg. About how many times as massive as the bacterium is the grain of sand?

steps: Write the comparison as a quotient: $\dfrac{7 \times 10^{-6}}{1 \times 10^{-12}}$.
Subtract the exponents, watching the signs: $10^{-6-(-12)} = 10^{-6+12} = 10^{6}$.
The grain of sand is about $7 \times 10^{6}$ times as massive as the bacterium.

items.prompt: A factory makes about $8 \times 10^{5}$ bottles each day and operates about $3 \times 10^{2}$ days each year. Estimate the number of bottles it makes per year. Write your answer as a single digit times a power of 10.

steps: The factory makes about $2.4 \times 10^{8}$ bottles per year.

items.prompt: The diameter of a virus is about $0.00000004$ m. Write this measurement as a single digit times an integer power of 10.

steps: The number is less than 1, so the power of 10 will be negative.
Move the decimal point to the right until it follows the first nonzero digit: $0.00000004 \to 4$.
Count the places moved: $8$ places to the right, so the exponent is $-8$.

items.prompt: A national park gets about $9 \times 10^{6}$ visitors per year. A small local park gets about $3 \times 10^{4}$ visitors per year. About how many times as many visitors does the national park get?

steps: Write the comparison as a quotient: $\dfrac{9 \times 10^{6}}{3 \times 10^{4}}$.
The national park gets about $3 \times 10^{2} = 300$ times as many visitors.

items.prompt: Light travels about $3 \times 10^{8}$ m in one second. Estimate how far light travels in about $6 \times 10^{1}$ seconds (one minute). Write your answer as a single digit times a power of 10.

steps: Multiply distance per second by the number of seconds: $(3 \times 10^{8})(6 \times 10^{1})$.
Light travels about $1.8 \times 10^{10}$ m in one minute.

items.prompt: A country produces about $4 \times 10^{6}$ metric tons of wheat, while a neighboring country produces about $8 \times 10^{8}$ metric tons. About how many times as much wheat does the neighbor produce?

steps: Write the comparison as a quotient with the larger amount on top: $\dfrac{8 \times 10^{8}}{4 \times 10^{6}}$.
The neighbor produces about $2 \times 10^{2} = 200$ times as much wheat.

items.prompt: The thickness of a sheet of paper is about $0.0001$ m. The diameter of a single atom is about $1 \times 10^{-10}$ m. About how many times as thick as an atom is the sheet of paper?

steps: First write the paper thickness as a power of 10: $0.0001 = 1 \times 10^{-4}$ m (the decimal moves 4 places right).
Write the comparison as a quotient: $\dfrac{1 \times 10^{-4}}{1 \times 10^{-10}}$.
Subtract the exponents, watching the signs: $10^{-4-(-10)} = 10^{-4+10} = 10^{6}$.
The sheet of paper is about $1 \times 10^{6}$ times as thick as an atom.

items.prompt: An online video gets about $5 \times 10^{7}$ views. Each viewer watches for about $2 \times 10^{2}$ seconds on average. Estimate the total number of seconds the video was watched. Write your answer as a single digit times a power of 10.

steps: Multiply views by seconds per view: $(5 \times 10^{7})(2 \times 10^{2})$.
The video was watched for about $1 \times 10^{10}$ seconds in total.

items.prompt: The mass of the Moon is about $7 \times 10^{22}$ kg, and the mass of the Earth is about $6 \times 10^{24}$ kg. About how many times as massive as the Moon is the Earth? Round your leading digit to the nearest whole number.

steps: Write the comparison as a quotient: $\dfrac{6 \times 10^{24}}{7 \times 10^{22}}$.
Round the leading digit and express in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form: about $9 \times 10^{1}$.
The Earth is about $9 \times 10^{1} \approx 90$ times as massive as the Moon.

items.prompt: A drop of water has a volume of about $5 \times 10^{-5}$ L. A large tank holds about $1 \times 10^{3}$ L. About how many drops of water would it take to fill the tank?

steps: Divide the tank volume by the volume of one drop: $\dfrac{1 \times 10^{3}}{5 \times 10^{-5}}$.
Subtract the exponents, watching the signs: $10^{3-(-5)} = 10^{3+5} = 10^{8}$.
It would take about $2 \times 10^{7}$ drops to fill the tank.

items.prompt: A computer performs about $2 \times 10^{9}$ operations per second. Estimate how many operations it performs in about $4 \times 10^{3}$ seconds. Write your answer as a single digit times a power of 10.

steps: Multiply operations per second by the number of seconds: $(2 \times 10^{9})(4 \times 10^{3})$.
The leading factor is already a single digit, so the answer is $8 \times 10^{12}$ operations.
